one_month_reasoning: Window to 2026-11-04. Inside it: (1) the Q2 FY27 report, the first continuing-operations guide for RemainCo. Modine has not yet announced the date (no notice on EDGAR as of Oct 6 [36]). Q1 was reported Jul 29 and Q2 FY26 on Oct 29, 2025 [29], so late October is very likely. It tests whether DC margins recover from Q1's 14.8% ($51.7M on $348.6M [30]) and whether DC sales re-accelerate after Q1 fell sequentially from Q4's $401.9M [32]. (2) Hyperscaler Q3 capex guides in late October [16]. (3) The 8-K/A pro forma, due about Oct 7 [37]. The Nov 18 Investor Day [34] falls just outside the window, but anticipation of new targets may limit downside after the print. MOD's earnings reactions are large and lean negative (-7.4% Q2 FY26 [13], about -17% in the Q1 FY27 week [7]), and the reset guide will sit mechanically below the old consolidated $650-680M because PT is removed [30], which could read badly at first glance. Against that, the DC '>85% earnings growth' guide [31] gives a bar that is plausible to reaffirm. With no edge on the sign, I keep the centre at about $183.5 with monthly sigma about 19% (71%/3.5 = 20%) and a 15% fat-tail component for the gap. This is unchanged from round 1. The supervisor's review agreed with the neutral stance and gave no new in-window fact that changes the sign.

fair_value.method: 12-month-forward value of RemainCo (Data Centers + Commercial HVAC). 60% weight on EV/EBITDA: 17.5x NTM-at-Oct-2027 EBITDA of $665M = EV $11.64B, less ~$150M net debt, over 54.0M diluted shares = $213. 40% weight on P/E: 25x NTM EPS of $7.88 = $197. Blended about $207 (+13% vs $182.91). Corporate cost is now -$80M/yr (Q1 actual -$23.0M/qtr).

Q1 FY27 run-rate -$23.0M/qtr (-$92M annualised) vs -$62.6M in FY26. Some of the Q1 cost is separation-related overhead that PT reimburses through the TSA, so I use about -$80M. This replaces round 1's -$65-85M range and no longer relies on the secondary 'no stranded costs' recap.

Bottom-up: DC $1.85B (+67%, low half of the +60-80% guide given the Q1 sequential dip) x 18.5% = $342M; CHVAC $1.06B (+9%) x 16.5% = $175M; corporate -$80M; total $437M. Guide-implied: DC earnings growth >85% gives >=$397M, plus CHVAC ~$175M, less $80M = ~$492M. I weight bottom-up 60/40: 0.6 x $437M + 0.4 x $492M = $459M (corrected from $455M, an arithmetic slip). This is below the explicit DC earnings guide because hitting it needs ~23% DC margin in Q2-Q4 after 14.8% in Q1.

DC +40% to $2.59B at 19.5% = $505M; CHVAC +7% to $1.13B at 16.5% = $187M; corporate -$82M. DC growth is below management's 50-70% two-year view. It is supported by the $4B CY27-29 capacity agreement (10-K [33]: 'more than $4 billion ... during calendar years 2027 through 2029'; ~$1.33B/yr = $4B / 3, an estimate) and the internal base case of 2027 customer AI capex +50% [16].
DC +20% (2028 customer capex base case +22% [16]) to $3.11B at 19.5% = $606M; CHVAC +7% at 16.5% = $200M; corporate -$85M.

On one formula (TTM EV/EBITDA from each peer's 10-Q/10-K and the Oct-5 close / (1+3Y consensus EPS CAGR)) the 10-peer median is 19.75x (range 11.2-27.11x). On a revenue-CAGR divisor the median is 20.73x and on the average divisor 20.23x. Taking ~20.23x as the reconciled midpoint, 17.5x is a ~13% discount and sits inside the range. The discount rests on persistent factors: one customer is ~11% of consolidated sales, ~30% of DC if all DC (estimate from [33]: 0.11 x $3,181.1M / $1,108.2M), and the $4B agreement runs through CY2029; DC margin is 19.4% in FY26 and 14.8% in Q1 versus VRT/NVT at ~22% (TTM GAAP EBITDA margins to 2026-06-30, 10-Q XBRL); and repeated supply-driven misses [7,30]. MOD trades at ~18x NTM today, so this assumes no re-rating. [Citation audit 2026-10-06: peer multiples re-derived from filings (EV from 10-Q debt/cash/shares and Oct-5 closes; TTM GAAP EBITDA) and consensus growth/EPS; aggregator multiples no longer used. The chosen multiple is unchanged.]

Jun-30 net debt $432.9M [30] less the $155,991,275 Cash Distribution [1] = $277M. Add part of the $25-35M transaction costs [31], giving ~$290M at close. The supervisor's ~$280M agrees, and the Cash Transfer offsets the PT cash. Less NTM FCF of ~$140M (EBITDA ~$530M - capex ~$180M - tax ~$85M - interest ~$15M - WC ~$90M - residual deal costs ~$20M).

53.20M basic at the record date: Modine Form 4 of 2026-10-05 reports 53,197,549 SpinCo shares distributed one-for-one to Sep-28 holders [39] (cross-check 23,735,961 THRM / 0.44619 [1]). Q1 FY27 diluted weighted shares were 54.0M [30].
EBITDA $665M - D&A ~$90M (rising with $150-200M/yr capex [31]) - interest ~$15M = $560M pre-tax x 0.76 = $426M / 54.0M shares.

The 10-peer forward P/E median is 25.93x (range 14.18-29.54x), each = Oct-5 close / NTM consensus EPS calendarised from stockanalysis this-year and next-year estimates (JCI's FY Sep-2027 is exactly NTM; CSWI blends FY Mar-27 and Mar-28). 25x is a ~4% discount, consistent in direction with the EV/EBITDA discount and for the same structural reasons. [Citation audit 2026-10-06: peer multiples re-derived from filings (EV from 10-Q debt/cash/shares and Oct-5 closes; TTM GAAP EBITDA) and consensus growth/EPS; aggregator multiples no longer used. The chosen multiple is unchanged.]

bear.story: AI capex digestion or a hyperscaler pause, recurring supply and margin misses, or share loss to VRT/TT/JCI. The Q2 reset or the Nov 18 targets disappoint. NTM EBITDA ~$520M x 13.5x (CARR/SPXC level) less ~$300M net debt = ~$124. Kalshi prices a 2027 recession at 20% [9].

base.story: DC grows ~40% in FY28 on the $4B agreement, DC margin recovers to ~19.5%, corporate is about -$80M, and the multiple holds at ~17.5x NTM EBITDA of ~$665M.

bull.story: DC grows at management's 50-70% pace, margins pass 20%, and NTM EBITDA reaches ~$800M. The multiple goes to ~20.5x, the upper half of the peer range but below VRT's 25.9x: (800 x 20.5 - 100) / 54 = ~$302. Round 1's bull needed 22x on $850M; I have cut it per the supervisor's review.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: There is no premium. The small discount rests on factors that persist through Oct-2027, with evidence: (1) concentration: one customer is ~11% of consolidated FY26 sales [33] (~30% of DC if all DC, an estimate), and the $4B capacity agreement locks that in through CY2029 [33]; (2) DC EBITDA margin of 19.4% in FY26 and 14.8% in Q1 FY27 [30,32], below VRT/NVT; (3) repeated supply and ramp misses [7,30]. Basis: forward P/E is the Oct-5 close over NTM consensus EPS calendarised from this-year/next-year estimates (exactly NTM for JCI; CSWI blends its March fiscal years). The forward EV/EBITDA figures are derived, not consensus.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$125 (-32%) the EV would be ~$7.0B (125 x 54.0M + ~$290M net debt). That is ~11.5x FY28E EBITDA of $610M and ~15x FY27E of $459M, which implies FY28 EBITDA with little growth from FY27, against DC guided +60-80% this year [31]. Such a level would most likely mean the $4B capacity agreement or DC share is impaired, or AI capex has turned down, rather than ordinary 71%-vol noise. It also equals my bear-scenario value.
